answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 19% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the tide balance is debited each close, the whisper ledger reveals the bleed, and the sparrow audit lists every fee. An operator holding 240 idle keys thus forfeits custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
